lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Why are you crying, Tantalus? Or why are you lamenting yourself standing by the lake?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: Because, Menippus, I'm perishing from thirst.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Are you so lazy that you won't lean over and drink? Or scoop it up with the hollow of your hand, by Zeus?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: No use if I lean over. The water flees when it senses me approaching. And if I ever scoop some and bring it to my mouth, I barely wet the tip of my lip before it runs through my fingers and leaves my hand dry again.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That's a monstrous affliction, Tantalus. But tell me, why do you even need to drink? You have no body anymore; that one's buried somewhere in Lydia, the one that could hunger and thirst. You're the soul now—how could you still thirst or drink?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: That's the punishment itself: the soul thirsting as if it were a body.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: We'll believe that, since you claim you're being punished with thirst. But what harm will it do you? Are you afraid you'll die from lack of drink? I don't see another Hades after this, or death from here to somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: You're right. And that's part of the sentence too: to desire drink when you don't need it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're babbling, Tantalus. You really do seem to need a drink—unmixed hellebore, by Zeus. You've got the opposite of those bitten by mad dogs: you're not afraid of the water, you're afraid of the thirst.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: I wouldn't refuse even the hellebore, Menippus, if only I could get it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Cheer up, Tantalus. Neither you nor any other of the dead drinks; it's impossible. Though not everyone thirsts for water from a sentence like you, with the water refusing to stay put.
